answer: Per-epoch nullifiers tie each earning seat to one scarce credential. An operator holds a credential, such as a hardware security key, and each epoch derives a cipher, a one-way nullifier from that key and the epoch number. The ledger accepts one cipher per credential per epoch, so a second seat from the same key collides and both are voided. The saffron list names issuers that charge per key and refuse bulk orders. A fable, a seat whose new key later traces to a reused one, is slashed. Each fake needs its own costly key, proven again every epoch.
